title: Pay for funerals and how it was spent
summary: Funeral pay is five to seven dollars with the leader getting more; it was two dollars when he arrived. He spent much on drink and also played nightly dances.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Let me see. How much does it pay?

Well, they pay, I believe, six to five dollars, six to five or seven dollars, seven dollars. I know when they went out, you know, they're going to give you six dollars on the man, except the leader, of course, you know, they get more.
The leader gets more, huh? What about the manager? Does he get more?
Well, he's here, I guess, them guys, they split it up, I guess.
What about when you first came here, how much were they paying for funerals then?
I mean, just two dollars, two and a half.
Well, how much of that money would you keep? I mean, by the time you got home?
Yeah, how much do I keep?
Yeah, well, I mean, you got to feed. All of it. All of it, and you'd go straight home?
I'd have it in there.
You mean, so you'd go straight home after you played a few hours? He said he'd have it in here.
I see. It's gone, and I guess the price of drinking's gone up in the years in between.

Well, let me tell you one thing. You see, I and Al, right now, but I mean, you know, when I was at the event, when we go on the film, we just go on there, just to be on there, just to have fun. You see, when we get home, we might have two dollars or three dollars out of the six, because we didn't drink the other part up.
Well, you strictly couldn't support yourself that way, could you?

Well, you see, we didn't depend on that for youngster and, no, not for youngster. Me, I read, I used to play them job. I just like to be in the street. I used to love the job, understand the bean and the street, you know, just play a few on the parade. But when I used to go play, we'd just go play there so we could drink, but for anything else, you know.
Well, in the old days, did any of the guys support themselves by playing in brass bands only?

Well, no, they couldn't exactly, just in brass bands only. Some of them used to play at night, but they didn't, they didn't play in the brass bands. Because myself, I used to play in the music box every night. That was on Cronlade and St. Charles, a jitney dance. And I used to play it every night, but in the film, sometimes we'd have a film every day, putting it. And I was like, well, you see, I just started. But of course, at that time when I was playing, I played in the middle of the way, I couldn't drink. Like I couldn't, I asked for that instant, but just nothing. Because I had to work at night, then work at night. You know, you couldn't, you couldn't make it that way. You just drinking and wasting all night. And I walked in the middle.
Well, it seems to me some of the people I know could play a funeral or parade and end up losing money, you know? I mean they could come out in the hole, huh? That would happen, huh?
Well, if you're going to suck it up, what do you expect? You got to lose.
I've seen that happen.
Yeah.
